title: Trigger Flag Allowlist Schema
description: Schema for .claude/metadata/trigger-flag-allowlist.json — per-command declaration of the flags workflow-trigger.js recognizes when routing a bare phrase to a slash command. Extraction from prompt text is governed by token shape; this allowlist governs whether a recognized flag may consume the following token as its value.

version.description: Schema revision of this data file

commands.description: Map of slash command name to the flags that command recognizes. A command present with an empty array declares that it accepts no flags — distinct from a command being absent, which means the routing path has never been reviewed for flag support.

additionalProperties.description: Recognized flags for this command, each in long form. An entry is EITHER a plain string — the original shape, meaning the flag claims exactly one following token — OR an object naming the flag and its attachment mode (#2770). The union is what keeps every entry written before #2770 valid and unchanged in meaning; the two shapes may be mixed freely within one command's array.

oneOf.description: Long-form flag claiming exactly one following token as its value. Equivalent to {"flag": "--x", "attach": "token"}.
Long-form flag with an explicit attachment mode.

attach.description: How much of the prompt this flag claims as its value. `token` (the default, and the meaning of a plain string entry) claims exactly one following token — correct for --with security, --mode solo, --assignee @me. `rest-of-line` claims every remaining token, which is what lets a flag take prose rather than a single value; /proposal --update is the motivating case, where `--update rename the risk section` previously bound only `rename` and returned the rest to the issue title. A `rest-of-line` value STOPS AT THE NEXT FLAG-SHAPED TOKEN, so `--update rewrite the intro --assignee octocat` binds `rewrite the intro` and leaves --assignee to claim its own value. That termination is not a convenience: extraction is governed by token shape, and Reference/GitHub-Workflow.md guarantees no flag-shaped token is ever silently discarded, so absorbing a following flag into prose would break that guarantee one level down — the same defect at the value layer that rest-of-line exists to fix. The `--flag=value` form carries its own value and never claims following tokens, whatever the declared attachment.
